bug_semantics: The Vision Chat paste-image handler derives the uploaded PNG filename from MD5(PIL.Image.tobytes()). PIL tobytes() serializes pixel or palette-index bytes but omits image dimensions, mode, palette, and transparency metadata, so visually different palette images can share the same digest and filename. In a shared instance, a second upload can overwrite the first file, and the vision model later fetches attacker-controlled content through the unchanged file URL.
flaw_origin: Upstream Langchain-Chatchat PR #4421 added multimodal image chat. Decomposing its squashed merge ee1912a2725c747942cad7290f7e5c38d1c1a88e identifies member commit 6699379d6673585a8010a2a9b20807bdb0bfbda8 as the smallest public commit that introduced the paste-image handler and the vulnerable hashlib.md5(paste_image.image_data.tobytes()) filename construction; its immediate parent lacks that construction.
ai_marker: absent: BIC commit 6699379d6673585a8010a2a9b20807bdb0bfbda8 has author and committer liunux4odoo <liunux@qq.com>; its complete commit message has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI marker
evidence: CVE.org record CVE-2026-7845 is PUBLISHED and identifies versions 0.3.1.0 through 0.3.1.3 as affected; it is not rejected or withdrawn.

GitHub issue https://github.com/chatchat-space/Langchain-Chatchat/issues/5462 documents the exact line libs/chatchat-server/chatchat/webui_pages/dialogue/dialogue.py:278 and the palette-metadata collision/overwrite chain; its only comments and closure were stale-bot automation, with no vendor fix or false-positive disposition.

GitHub PR API for https://github.com/chatchat-space/Langchain-Chatchat/pull/4421 reports 10 member commits, base 5d9763aead88f36e5d606b276bf0365249954e9e, head d75d2b9177b406d88a471ed69d00d0b5eb929e4a, and squashed merge ee1912a2725c747942cad7290f7e5c38d1c1a88e.

PR-member commit 6699379d6673585a8010a2a9b20807bdb0bfbda8 modifies libs/chatchat-server/chatchat/webui_pages/dialogue/dialogue.py and adds hashlib, paste_image_button, upload_image_file, and the exact line name = hashlib.md5(paste_image.image_data.tobytes()).hexdigest()+".png".

Direct parent-tree retrieval at 3c43f737948d12b7ac6b19878a38759232fbc92c returns the same source path but no hashlib.md5(paste_image.image_data.tobytes()) occurrence; the occurrence is present at child 6699379d6673585a8010a2a9b20807bdb0bfbda8 line 279.
The complete BIC commit object names human author and committer liunux4odoo <liunux@qq.com> and contains no AI/bot identity or AI-related trailer.

Release tag v0.3.0 lacks the vulnerable expression; squashed carrier ee1912a2725c747942cad7290f7e5c38d1c1a88e is 61 commits after v0.3.0, and tag v0.3.1 at a6a9193b5002061719f0eee62c6310bd5b1b7f63 is 69 commits after the carrier and contains the vulnerable expression at line 280.
Upstream master HEAD 49165d6af4438aa7e8a1f71ce276db55f4405151 still contains the vulnerable expression at line 278, so no direct fix is present in current public upstream history.

The assigned disclosure clone is full-history and non-shallow. Its report commit 58b5c1aba218aec104463c83ca594bbe13ff237a has a Claude Opus 4.6 Co-Authored-By trailer, but that commit only adds the later vulnerability report in 3em0/cve_repo and is not the product-code BIC.
reasoning: The advisory describes a real content-identity flaw rather than an ordinary MD5 cryptanalytic collision: hashing only PIL raw pixel/index bytes omits palette and other PNG semantics, allowing different rendered images to map to one server filename and enabling overwrite before model fetch. History was traced from the vulnerable line, not from the AI-marked disclosure. PR #4421's squash carrier first placed the feature on upstream master, and decomposition shows that member 6699379d6673585a8010a2a9b20807bdb0bfbda8 is the atomic writer; its immediate parent has the file but not the vulnerable line. The carrier precedes and is contained in affected v0.3.1, while v0.3.0 lacks the line. Because the atomic BIC's author, committer, full message, and trailers contain no AI marker, the real vulnerability is NOT_AI. The later Claude-coauthored report cannot transfer AI authorship to the earlier BIC. No public fix exists: the issue was closed only by stale automation and current master retains the expression.

potential_fix.approach: Serialize the complete image to canonical PNG bytes and derive a collision-resistant content identifier from those bytes, while also preventing silent replacement of an existing stored object.
potential_fix.rationale: Hashing the complete encoded image includes dimensions, palette, transparency, and other rendering-relevant data that PIL tobytes() omits; rejecting filename collisions or using immutable unique storage removes the overwrite/TOCTOU primitive even if an identifier collision occurs.
